CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kubu Raya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government Administrator who leads the Implementation of Government Affairs that are the Authority of the Autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Kubu Raya.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an Organization or institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent.
5. Women are humans who are female starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women with Disabilities are women who have limitations, which can be physical, cognitive, mental, sensory, emotional, developmental or some combination of these.
7. Elderly Women are women who are 60 years of age and above.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including certain threats, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the regional government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Service/handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
14. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.
18. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
20. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the State to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

CHAPTER II
SCOPE OF PROTECTION
Article 4
The scope of protection of women from acts of violence includes:
a. prevention;
b. services and/or handling; and
c. empowerment.

Article 19
Other violence as referred to in Article 13 letter f includes: a. any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
b. a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER VI
INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER
Article 25
(1) In providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house (shelter) for victims, it is necessary to establish a PPT.
(2) PPT may be established by vertical agencies in the Region, Regional Government, and/or community institutions.
(3) PPT established by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of elements of the Regional Police, SKPD responsible for Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions that have the function of providing protection to women from acts of violence carried out in a networked manner.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (1), then the victim shall be referred to a PPT that has a safe house.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of several counseling fields including:
a. legal field;
b. health field;
c. spiritual field; and
d. psychological field.
(6) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

Article 16
Sexual violence as referred to in Article 13 letter c includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUBU RAYA REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

Article 18
Exploitation as referred to in Article 13 letter e includes:
a. actions that exploit women economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others.
b. actions with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, violence, physical exploitation, sexual exploitation, exploitation of reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Article 14
Physical violence as referred to in Article 13 letter a includes acts that result in pain, wounds, injury or disability to the body, miscarriage, fainting, and/or death.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.
Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access and welfare.
What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, regional government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, must prioritize the best interests of victims.

Article 24
(1) Services and/or handling for victims are carried out in a networked manner.
(2) The network as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to:
a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of PPT services;
b. develop networks and referral systems; and
c. collect, compile and present reports on violence.
(3) The network as referred to in paragraph (1) carries out its duties and functions in accordance with the forms of services as referred to in Article 7.

CHAPTER X
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 29
(1) Regional Government conducts development and supervision of the implementation of women's protection.
(2) Development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers planning and implementation.
(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers planning, implementation, governance, financing, quality, control, and supervision.
(5) Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(6) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted based on laws and regulations periodically every 6 (six) months.

Article 15

Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.

22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUBU RAYA REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kubu Raya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government Administrator who leads the Implementation of Government Affairs that are the Authority of the Autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Kubu Raya.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an Organization or institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent.
5. Women are humans who are female starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women with Disabilities are women who have limitations, which can be physical, cognitive, mental, sensory, emotional, developmental or some combination of these.
7. Elderly Women are women who are 60 years of age and above.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including certain threats, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the regional government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Service/handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
14. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.
18. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
20. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the State to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUBU RAYA REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

REGENT OF KUBU RAYA
DECIDES:
To Establish REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.

15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. 23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kubu Raya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government Administrator who leads the Implementation of Government Affairs that are the Authority of the Autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Kubu Raya.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an Organization or institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent.
5. Women are humans who are female starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women with Disabilities are women who have limitations, which can be physical, cognitive, mental, sensory, emotional, developmental or some combination of these.
7. Elderly Women are women who are 60 years of age and above.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including certain threats, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the regional government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Service/handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
14. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.
18. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
20. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the State to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

Article 24
(1) Services and/or handling for victims are carried out in a networked manner.
(2) The network as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to:
a. coordinate and synchronize the handling of PPT services;
b. develop networks and referral systems; and
c. collect, compile and present reports on violence.
(3) The network as referred to in paragraph (1) carries out its duties and functions in accordance with the forms of services as referred to in Article 7.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kubu Raya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government Administrator who leads the Implementation of Government Affairs that are the Authority of the Autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Kubu Raya.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an Organization or institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent.
5. Women are humans who are female starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women with Disabilities are women who have limitations, which can be physical, cognitive, mental, sensory, emotional, developmental or some combination of these.
7. Elderly Women are women who are 60 years of age and above.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including certain threats, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the regional government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Service/handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
14. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.
18. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
20. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the State to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

SCOPE OF PROTECTION
Article 4
The scope of protection of women from acts of violence includes:
a. prevention;
b. services and/or handling; and
c. empowerment.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUBU RAYA REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

CHAPTER VI
INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER
Article 25
(1) In providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house (shelter) for victims, it is necessary to establish a PPT.
(2) PPT may be established by vertical agencies in the Region, Regional Government, and/or community institutions.
(3) PPT established by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of elements of the Regional Police, SKPD responsible for Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions that have the function of providing protection to women from acts of violence carried out in a networked manner.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (1), then the victim shall be referred to a PPT that has a safe house.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of several counseling fields including:
a. legal field;
b. health field;
c. spiritual field; and
d. psychological field.
(6) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

CHAPTER X
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 29
(1) Regional Government conducts development and supervision of the implementation of women's protection.
(2) Development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. coordination;
b. guidance;
c. education and training; and
d. monitoring and evaluation.
(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2) letter a covers planning and implementation.
(4) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b covers planning, implementation, governance, financing, quality, control, and supervision.
(5) Education and training as referred to in paragraph (2) letter c shall be conducted in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
(6) Monitoring and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (2) letter d shall be conducted based on laws and regulations periodically every 6 (six) months.

Article 19
Other violence as referred to in Article 13 letter f includes: a. any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
b. a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 16
Sexual violence as referred to in Article 13 letter c includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual relations with another person for commercial purposes and/or specific purposes.

Article 18
Exploitation as referred to in Article 13 letter e includes:
a. actions that exploit women economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others.
b. actions with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, violence, physical exploitation, sexual exploitation, exploitation of reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including certain threats, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the regional government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Service/handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
14. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.
18. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.

20. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the State to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

Article 2

What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, regional government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, must prioritize the best interests of victims.

Article 19
Other violence as referred to in Article 13 letter f includes: a. any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
b. a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 18
Exploitation as referred to in Article 13 letter e includes:
a. actions that exploit women economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others.
b. actions with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, violence, physical exploitation, sexual exploitation, exploitation of reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kubu Raya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government Administrator who leads the Implementation of Government Affairs that are the Authority of the Autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Kubu Raya.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an Organization or institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent.
5. Women are humans who are female starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women with Disabilities are women who have limitations, which can be physical, cognitive, mental, sensory, emotional, developmental or some combination of these.
7. Elderly Women are women who are 60 years of age and above.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including certain threats, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the regional government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Service/handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
14. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.
18. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
20. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the State to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUBU RAYA REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kubu Raya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government Administrator who leads the Implementation of Government Affairs that are the Authority of the Autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Kubu Raya.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an Organization or institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent.
5. Women are humans who are female starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women with Disabilities are women who have limitations, which can be physical, cognitive, mental, sensory, emotional, developmental or some combination of these.
7. Elderly Women are women who are 60 years of age and above.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including certain threats, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the regional government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Service/handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
14. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.
18. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
20. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the State to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUBU RAYA REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

CHAPTER VI
INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER
Article 25
(1) In providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house (shelter) for victims, it is necessary to establish a PPT.
(2) PPT may be established by vertical agencies in the Region, Regional Government, and/or community institutions.
(3) PPT established by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of elements of the Regional Police, SKPD responsible for Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions that have the function of providing protection to women from acts of violence carried out in a networked manner.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (1), then the victim shall be referred to a PPT that has a safe house.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of several counseling fields including:
a. legal field;
b. health field;
c. spiritual field; and
d. psychological field.
(6) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

Article 17
Neglect as referred to in Article 13 letter d includes: a. acts that neglect women within the scope of their household; and/or
b. acts that result in economic dependence.

CHAPTER VIII
FUNDING
Article 27
Funding for women's protection activities carried out by the Regional Government is sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and/or other legitimate sources in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 10
(1) Job training as referred to in Article 9 letter b includes:  a. skills training;
b. field work practice; and
c. apprenticeship.

Article 26
(1) The SKPD responsible for Women's Empowerment implements the information system and submits reports on the implementation of women's protection to the Regent.
(2) Further provisions regarding the information system and reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by the Regent's Regulation.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Article 4
The scope of protection of women from acts of violence includes:
a. prevention;

c. empowerment.

25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUBU RAYA REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

CHAPTER VI
INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER
Article 25
(1) In providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house (shelter) for victims, it is necessary to establish a PPT.
(2) PPT may be established by vertical agencies in the Region, Regional Government, and/or community institutions.
(3) PPT established by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of elements of the Regional Police, SKPD responsible for Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions that have the function of providing protection to women from acts of violence carried out in a networked manner.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (1), then the victim shall be referred to a PPT that has a safe house.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of several counseling fields including:
a. legal field;
b. health field;
c. spiritual field; and
d. psychological field.
(6) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be determined by Regent's Decree.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF KUBU RAYA REGENCY
NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

Article 17
Neglect as referred to in Article 13 letter d includes: a. acts that neglect women within the scope of their household; and/or
b. acts that result in economic dependence.

NUMBER ... YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL.
Acts of violence against women constitute a violation of human rights; therefore, their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and innate nature, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

In order to prevent and overcome violence against women in Kubu Raya Regency so that they are protected from violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades the degree and dignity of humanity, it is necessary to establish a regional regulation concerning the protection of women.
Protection of women constitutes all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention.
Existing laws and regulations or those related to the protection of women victims of violence have not yet regulated efforts for the protection of women in the regions; therefore, institutional support and regulations at the regional level are needed to guarantee their implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates efforts for the protection of women, specifically in the form of prevention, services/handling, and empowerment of women in Kubu Raya Regency.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kubu Raya Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government Administrator who leads the Implementation of Government Affairs that are the Authority of the Autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Kubu Raya.
4. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is an Organization or institution in the regional government that is responsible to the Regent.
5. Women are humans who are female starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly.
6. Women with Disabilities are women who have limitations, which can be physical, cognitive, mental, sensory, emotional, developmental or some combination of these.
7. Elderly Women are women who are 60 years of age and above.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
9. Violence against women is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering to women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including certain threats, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
10. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence and life vulnerability.
11. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the regional government, community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against victims will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
12. Service/handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
13. Assistance is a person or group/team from an institution that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and/or advocacy.
14. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution or functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
15. Safe House is a place of residence for victims during the assistance process for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers.
16. Minimum Service Standards, hereinafter abbreviated as SPM, is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing 5 (five) types of services for women and children victims of violence, namely (1) Complaint Handling, (2) Health Services, (3) Social Rehabilitation, (4) Law Enforcement and Legal Aid, and (5) Repatriation and Social Reintegration.
17. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women submitted by victims, families and the community.
18. Health Services are efforts that include promotive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
19. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can perform their social functions properly.
20. Law Enforcement is action by officials authorized by the State to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocacy to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women that is gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment for victims.
24. Integrated Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPT, is a unified unit that performs integrated service functions for women victims of violence.
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in one straight line upward or downward.
26. Household is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations due to blood relations, marriage, milk kinship, care and guardianship and/or domestic workers who reside in that household.

Article 18
Exploitation as referred to in Article 13 letter e includes:
a. actions that exploit women economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others.
b. actions with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, violence, physical exploitation, sexual exploitation, exploitation of reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "respect and fulfillment of victims' rights" is the guarantee of the fulfillment of victims' basic rights.
Letter b What is meant by "justice" is a condition where every person, both men and women, are treated equally and obtain equal opportunities to gain access and welfare.
What is meant by "gender equality" is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.
Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, regional government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, must prioritize the best interests of victims.

(3) Further provisions regarding the development, mechanism, and working relationship of integrated PPT networks as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18
Exploitation as referred to in Article 13 letter e includes:
a. actions that exploit women economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others.
b. actions with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, violence, physical exploitation, sexual exploitation, exploitation of reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or exploiting the labor or capabilities of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
c. all forms of exploitation of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

a. entrepreneurial skills training; and

CHAPTER VI
INTEGRATED SERVICE CENTER
Article 25
(1) In providing services and temporary protection in the form of a safe house (shelter) for victims, it is necessary to establish a PPT.
(2) PPT may be established by vertical agencies in the Region, Regional Government, and/or community institutions.
(3) PPT established by the Regional Government as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of elements of the Regional Police, SKPD responsible for Health, Education, Social Affairs, Community Empowerment, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as well as Community Social Institutions that have the function of providing protection to women from acts of violence carried out in a networked manner.
(4) In the event that PPT does not have a safe house (shelter) as referred to in paragraph (1), then the victim shall be referred to a PPT that has a safe house.
(5) PPT as referred to in paragraph (2) consists of several counseling fields including:

b. health field;
c. spiritual field; and
d. psychological field.
